value.body: An in-house designer works inside one company — a product firm, retailer, fashion brand, publisher or manufacturer — designing for that company's own products and brand. Roles include UX/UI, product or industrial design, communication / graphic design and fashion design. In-house work gives depth on one brand; agency or studio work gives variety across many clients.

items.label: Common titles
items.note: Titles vary by company and industry

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Des, or another degree or diploma in design, and a portfolio of real work. Companies hire through campus placements, job postings and referrals; internships often lead to full-time offers.

value.title: At a glance
items: In-house: one brand, longer projects, close work with engineering, marketing or merchandising teams.
Agency or studio: many clients, faster turnaround, more variety.
Hiring decisions lean heavily on the portfolio.
